text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Scores of visa applicants stranded as British high commission suspends processing of their applications pending improvement in public electricity supply to its visa office.
- Nigeria's naira currency appreciates by 50 kobo because of increase in foreign reserves, says central bank officials.
- The Nigeria-Mobil joint venture signs $125 million contract with French firm Bouygues S.A. to supply three new platforms lay six pipelines for its natural gas liquids project.
- Britain says it will not accept a General Sani Abacha presidency should the Nigerian military ruler contest and win next year's presidential election aimed at restoring democracy.
- All pending by-elections from the March local council poll will take place on July 31, says the electoral commission.
- Motorists claim that petrol imported to end a recent fuel shortage in Nigeria burns 25 percent faster and has therefore increased their fuel expenditure.
- Shell denies it is responsible for 500 barrels of oil that spilled into farmlands in the volatile Ogoniland.
- Northern Kaduna state dismisses its entire workforce because of their current strike action.
- Opposition leaders press for continued suspension of Nigeria from Commonwealth at their meeting in London with Commonwealth Ministerial Action Group.
- Nigerian naira currency appreciates again at weekly foreign exchange auction as demand falls to $36.525 million this week from $37.789 million last week.
